# How to Make Custom Magnetic Closure Boxes?

A step-by-step look at how magnetic closure boxes are made, from cutting the board to wrapping and fitting magnets.

By Sarah AshleyJuly 30, 2026

![How to Make Custom Magnetic Closure Boxes?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/how-to-make-custom-magnetic-closure-boxes.webp)

Unboxing today is a brand experience. It starts when customers see a sleek box and hear the satisfying click of a magnetic lid, and it shapes how they see your product and your brand. That is exactly what custom magnetic closure rigid boxes are designed to deliver. Here is what they are and how they are made.

## What Are Magnetic Closure Boxes?

[Magnetic closure boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/magnetic-closure-boxes/) are premium rigid boxes with magnets hidden in the flap for a secure, elegant close. They are used for luxury goods, gifts, cosmetics, electronics, apparel and PR kits, protecting products in storage and shipping while delivering a high-end presentation.

## How Magnetic Rigid Boxes Are Made

Making a magnetic box is a structural process: defining dimensions, choosing materials, printing, finishing and assembling.

### Step 1: Choose the materials

- Chipboard: the core structure. Options include greyboard, duplex chipboard and thick cardboard, typically 800–1400 GSM depending on product size and weight. See [what is rigid stock](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-rigid-stock/).
- Wrapping paper: carries the artwork and branding, in paperboard, kraft, textured or other specialty papers.
- Magnets: small but strong magnets for the closure.

Material choice affects the whole structure and look of the box, and careful selection helps control cost.

### Step 2: Choose collapsible or non-collapsible

Non-collapsible boxes stay assembled. Collapsible boxes fold flat when not in use to save space. Pick the one that suits your product and logistics.

### Step 3: Print the wrap

Artwork is printed digitally or, most often, with offset printing, which gives rich, consistent color using CMYK and Pantone (PMS).

### Step 4: Laminate and die-cut

The printed sheets are laminated in matte, gloss or soft-touch to protect the design, then die-cut to the exact shape needed to wrap the box.

### Step 5: Add finishes

- [Hot foil stamping](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-foil-stamping/) for metallic logos
- [Embossing](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-embossing/) or [debossing](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-debossing/) for tactile detail
- [Spot UV](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-spot-uv/) to highlight logos and patterns

### Step 6: Install the magnets

Shallow round recesses are cut into the board so the magnets sit flush, with no bumps. Strong neodymium disc magnets are glued into the front panel, and matching opposite-pole magnets or metal plates go inside the lid flap. Precise alignment gives a smooth, satisfying close every time.

## Collapsible vs Non-Collapsible

| Feature | Collapsible | Non-collapsible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structure | Ships flat, folds into shape | Pre-assembled, always holds its shape |
| Storage | Minimal space | More space |
| Shipping cost | Lower, since more fit per shipment | Higher, due to volume |
| Assembly | Quick assembly needed | Ready to use |
| Strength | Strong once assembled; fold lines visible | Maximum strength, seamless look |
| Best for | E-commerce, subscriptions, space-saving | Luxury retail, gifts, electronics, jewelry, cosmetics |

Comparing box families? Read [rigid boxes vs folding cartons vs corrugated](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/rigid-boxes-vs-folding-cartons-vs-corrugated/).

## Why Invest in Magnetic Boxes?

- Higher perceived value: the rigid build and magnetic click signal quality.
- Luxury with sustainability: they can be made with FSC-certified board, recyclable materials and water-based adhesives.
- Long-term marketing: customers keep and reuse them for jewelry, cosmetics and keepsakes, keeping your brand in view.

## Final Thoughts

Magnetic closure boxes combine durability, premium presentation and protection. Making them takes careful planning, quality materials and precise craftsmanship, and when it is done right, every order leaves a lasting impression.

Pack Legacy manufactures all types of [rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/) at wholesale prices. [Get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

# How To Measure Magnetic Closure Box Dimensions?

Measure length, width and depth the right way so your magnetic box and its insert fit your product perfectly.

By Sarah AshleyAugust 10, 2026

![How To Measure Magnetic Closure Box Dimensions?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/how-to-measure-magnetic-closure-box-dimensionsz.webp)

Size is one of the most important decisions when ordering custom [magnetic closure boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/magnetic-closure-boxes/). The right size keeps your product safe and presents it at its best. Here is why accurate measuring matters and how to measure a magnetic rigid box step by step.

## Why Accurate Measurements Matter

A well-sized box holds the product snugly, neither squeezed nor loose, so it stays safe even when handled roughly. Accurate dimensions also:

- Use the right amount of material
- Reduce waste and cost
- Make printing and design easier
- Give a better finished look

Curious how these boxes are built? Read [how custom magnetic closure boxes are made](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/how-to-make-custom-magnetic-closure-boxes/).

## Before You Measure: Understand the Style

A magnetic rigid box opens like a hinged box, with magnets holding the lid closed. The width and front panel height need special attention so the closure is strong and secure, while the length supports the hinge.

You need three dimensions, Length × Width × Height, and one of these tools:

- Tape measure: good all-round for length, width and height.
- Ruler: best for small boxes and short dimensions.
- Yardstick: handy for large boxes.

## How to Measure a Magnetic Box

### Step 1: Length

Place the box on a flat surface and find its longest horizontal side. Measure edge to edge, keeping the tool straight and parallel to the edge, never diagonally.

### Step 2: Width

Measure from the front edge to the back edge, viewed from above, in a straight line between opposite edges. Use the same unit as the length.

### Step 3: Height

With the box assembled and upright, measure vertically from the bottom to the top edge, keeping the tool perpendicular to the base. Don’t measure the lid or flap separately for this.

### Step 4: Check the closure flap

Measure the flap that folds over the front panel separately. It should fully cover the closure area, and its magnets must line up with their partners. Its final size depends on the construction, board thickness, fold points, closure design and magnet placement.

## Inside vs Outside Dimensions

| Inside dimensions | Outside dimensions |
| --- | --- |
| The usable space inside the box | The full exterior size of the finished box |
| Best for checking the product fits | Best for the box’s overall footprint |
| Measured from the inside walls and base | Measured from the outermost edges |
| Exclude wall thickness | Include board, wrap and structure |
| Must allow for inserts, trays, dividers or foam | Usually unaffected by inserts |
| Use when building a box around a product | Use for shipping, storage and shelf planning |

## Common Measuring Mistakes

- Measuring only the outside
- Measuring unevenly or at an angle
- Forgetting the flap
- Ignoring material thickness
- Mixing units
- Not double-checking

## Need Help Measuring?

Our team can measure your box dimensions accurately so the finished box fits your product perfectly. Customize [rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/) at wholesale prices with free shipping, or [get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

## FAQs

### How do I calculate the volume of a magnetic box?

Multiply the three dimensions: Volume = Length × Width × Height.

### What order should I measure in?

Length × Width × Height: the longest side first, then the shorter side, then the vertical height with the box closed.

### Should I measure inside or outside?

Use inside dimensions when the product needs a specific fit, and outside dimensions when the finished box size matters.

### How do I measure a box with inserts?

Measure the space left after allowing for the insert’s thickness and position, so the product, insert and closure all have clearance.

### How do I measure the closure flap?

Open the box fully and measure from the flap’s fold line to its outer edge. It should cover the closure fully and align the magnets.

# Magnetic Closure Boxes: The Complete Guide to Types, Materials, Design & Uses

Everything about magnetic closure boxes: styles, rigid board options, finishes, inserts and the products they suit best.

By Sarah AshleyOctober 6, 2026

![Magnetic Closure Boxes: The Complete Guide to Types, Materials, Design & Uses](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/magnetic-closure-boxes-blog.webp)

Packaging is protection, presentation and customer experience in one, and magnetic closure boxes deliver all three. The satisfying snap of the magnet signals quality and reassures buyers that the product inside is secure. This guide covers the types, materials, structure, design, uses and costs of magnetic boxes.

## What Are Magnetic Closure Boxes?

[Magnetic closure boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/magnetic-closure-boxes/) are rigid or foldable boxes with magnets hidden in the flap or lid, giving a smooth, precise, premium close. Like other [rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/), they are valued for durability, elegance and a memorable unboxing, and are popular in luxury retail, cosmetics, electronics, gifting and subscriptions.

## Types of Magnetic Closure Boxes

- Rigid magnetic boxes: thick, non-collapsible chipboard with a premium feel, common for jewelry, perfume and electronics.
- Foldable magnetic boxes: ship flat and save storage, cost-efficient for e-commerce and subscriptions. See [collapsible rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/collapsible-rigid-boxes/).
- Book-style magnetic boxes: open like a hardcover, with room for inside printing and storytelling, ideal for cosmetics, collectibles and luxury sets. See [book boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/book-boxes/).
- Flip-top magnetic boxes: the lid lifts upward for a sleek, modern look, popular for tea, spirits and lifestyle products.

## Materials

- Chipboard or greyboard: thick, premium [rigid stock](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-rigid-stock/).
- Specialty wraps: matte, gloss, foil or pearlescent papers.
- Inserts: EVA foam, cardboard dividers or fabric lining.

## How a Magnetic Box Is Built

- Rigid base: thick chipboard or greyboard forms the strong main body.
- Lid with flap: the lid extends into a flap that folds over the front. Magnets in the flap and front wall snap it shut.
- Hidden magnets: embedded out of sight for a seamless look and a smoother close than a tuck-end box.
- Outer wrap: decorative paper or specialty finish covers the board, hides the magnets and carries your branding.
- Interior: an open cavity that can hold foam, cardboard or fabric inserts.
- Opening style: usually a front flap, with book-style (side opening) and flip-top variations.

See the full process in [how custom magnetic closure boxes are made](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/how-to-make-custom-magnetic-closure-boxes/).

## Design Features That Elevate Magnetic Boxes

- Custom printing: logo, brand colors and visuals outside, with inside printing for a surprise message or instructions. QR codes can link to tutorials or loyalty programs.
- Finishes: foil stamping, embossing, debossing and Spot UV. Foil on the flap, for example, highlights the closure. Read [choosing the perfect finish for your magnetic box](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/choosing-the-perfect-finish-for-your-magnetic-box/).
- Textures and laminations: soft-touch, gloss, matte or kraft for tactile appeal.
- Inserts and compartments: EVA foam, cardboard or fabric for protection and presentation.

## Sustainability

Buyers increasingly expect eco-friendly packaging. Magnetic boxes can use recyclable chipboard, kraft wraps and soy-based inks, and foldable designs reduce shipping volume and emissions. Because they are durable and attractive, customers often reuse them for storage, gifting or organizing, extending their life and reducing waste.

## Uses of Magnetic Closure Boxes

- Luxury retail: jewelry, watches and perfume.
- Cosmetics: skincare sets and makeup.
- Electronics: phones, accessories and premium gadgets.
- Food and beverage: teas, spirits and gourmet confectionery.
- Subscriptions: apparel and lifestyle products.
- Corporate gifting: [PR boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/pr-boxes/) and promotional gifts.

## Buyer Psychology and Unboxing

- Sensory impact: the snap, the smooth reveal and the tactile finish create an emotional connection.
- Social sharing: unboxing videos turn your packaging into free advertising.
- Perceived value: even mid-range products feel more prestigious.
- Loyalty: memorable unboxing encourages repeat purchases.
- Care: a well-designed box tells buyers you value them.

## Cost and Practical Considerations

- Material: rigid magnetic boxes cost more because of thick board and premium wraps; foldable versions use less material and ship flat.
- Production: embedding magnets and adding foil or embossing increases cost.
- Shipping and storage: foldable boxes save warehouse space and freight; rigid boxes take more room but offer unmatched durability.
- Sizing: oversized boxes waste material and shipping volume, so [measure your box correctly](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/how-to-measure-magnetic-closure-box-dimensions/).
- Positioning: luxury brands justify the cost through higher perceived value; mid-range products can use foldable boxes for a premium feel at lower cost.

## How to Choose the Right Magnetic Box

- Weight and size: heavy or bulky items need rigid boxes; smaller items can use foldable ones.
- Fragility: fragile items benefit from book-style boxes with inserts.
- Unboxing: book-style boxes allow storytelling inside; flip-tops give a sleek reveal.
- Customization: check which styles support the foil, embossing or inserts you want.

In short: choose rigid when prestige and durability matter most, and foldable when cost and shipping efficiency come first.

## Final Thought

Magnetic closure boxes tell stories, build trust and drive sales. Whether rigid, foldable, book-style or flip-top, the right box elevates your product and builds loyalty. Design around your product, brand and buyer, because packaging is the beginning of customer engagement, not the end. [Get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

### What are magnetic closure boxes?

Rigid or foldable boxes with hidden magnets in the flap or lid for a smooth, secure, premium close.

### Which products suit magnetic boxes?

Luxury items such as jewelry, perfume, electronics, cosmetics and premium gifts.

### How durable are they?

Very. Rigid board and hidden magnets give strength, long life and a secure closure.

### Are magnetic boxes cost-efficient?

Yes, especially foldable designs, which ship flat and save storage and logistics costs while still feeling premium.

# Measure Your Bakery Box Dimensions (A Complete 2026 Guide)

How to size boxes for cakes, cupcakes, cookies and pastries, with room for frosting, inserts and windows.

By Sarah AshleyJuly 20, 2026

![Measure Your Bakery Box Dimensions (A Complete 2026 Guide)](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/mesauring-sizes.webp)

Choosing the right bakery box size matters as much as the bake itself. The right box presents and protects your goods without wasting money. The wrong one causes three problems: damaged products, wasted material and unhappy customers. This guide covers standard bakery box sizes and how to measure boxes for cakes, cupcakes, cookies, donuts and more.

## Why Bakery Box Size Matters

Baked goods are delicate. A box that is too small crushes frosting and decorations, while one that is too big lets products slide around. The right size helps you:

- Protect the shape and decoration of your bakes
- Keep products secure in storage and delivery
- Reduce material waste and packaging costs
- Create a better shopping and unboxing experience
- Present your products professionally

For more on choosing boxes, read our [bakery packaging guide](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/bakery-packaging-guide/).

## Standard Bakery Box Sizes

| Box type | Size / capacity | Dimensions (in) | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cake | Small | 8 × 8 × 5 | 6″ round cake, with room for frosting |
| Cake | Medium | 10 × 10 × 5 | 8″ round cake |
| Cake | Large | 12 × 12 × 6 | 10″ round or 9″ square cake |
| Cake | Sheet | 14 × 10 × 4 | Quarter-sheet cake |
| Cupcake | Single | 4 × 4 × 4 | 1 cupcake (usually with a 2.5″ insert) |
| Cupcake | 4-count | 8 × 8 × 4 | 4 standard cupcakes |
| Cupcake | 6-count | 10 × 7 × 4 | Half dozen |
| Cupcake | 12-count | 14 × 10 × 4 | Full dozen |
| Cookie | Small | 6 × 6 × 2 | 4–6 gourmet cookies |
| Cookie | Medium | 8 × 8 × 2 | 12 standard cookies, laid flat |
| Cookie | Large | 10 × 10 × 3 | Assorted platters or gift box |
| Donut | Single / twin | 4 × 4 × 2.5 | 1–2 jumbo donuts |
| Donut | Half dozen | 9 × 6 × 3 | 6 standard donuts |
| Donut | Dozen | 12 × 12 × 3.5 | 12 donuts in one layer |
| Pastry | Small | 4 × 4 × 2 | Single croissant or Danish |
| Pastry | Medium | 9 × 6 × 3 | 3–4 éclairs, cannoli or slices |
| Pastry | Assorted | 10 × 8 × 3 | Catering mix or takeout |
| Pie | Small | 6 × 6 × 2 | Mini pies or tarts |
| Pie | Standard | 10 × 10 × 2.5 | 8″–9″ pie |
| Macaron | 6-pack | 6 × 3 × 2 | Single-row sleeve or window box |
| Macaron | 12-pack | 8 × 4 × 2 | Double row with insert |
| Panettone | Mini (100 g) | 4 × 4 × 4 | Individual sweet bread |
| Panettone | Medium (500 g) | 6.5 × 6.5 × 7 | Traditional tall panettone |
| Panettone | Large (1 kg) | 8 × 8 × 9 | Standard 1 kg panettone |

If your products don’t fit standard sizes, you’ll need [custom bakery boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/bakery-boxes/), measured correctly for a perfect fit.

## How to Measure a Bakery Box

1. Length: place the box on a flat surface and measure the longest side from inside edge to inside edge.
2. Width: measure the shorter side, again from inside edge to inside edge.
3. Height: stand the box upright and measure from the inside bottom to the inside top edge.
4. Record them in order: Length × Width × Height. A box 10″ long, 8″ wide and 4″ high is 10″ × 8″ × 4″.
5. Double-check: measure each side again before you order. Small errors lead to boxes that are too tight or too loose.

For other products, see our general guide to [measuring box dimensions](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/measure-your-box-dimensions/).

## Measuring Different Bakery Boxes

### Cake boxes

Measure the inside length, width and height, leaving room for frosting and decorations. Height is especially important for tall or layered cakes.

### Cupcake boxes

Measure length and width, then height. If you use inserts, match the holes to your cupcake diameter and spacing, and leave enough clearance to protect the frosting.

### Cookie boxes

Cookie boxes are shallow, so length and width matter most. For stacked cookies, increase the height to suit the stack.

### Panettone boxes

These are taller than most bakery boxes. Measure the inside carefully, especially the height, to leave space above the loaf.

### Donut boxes

Size the length and width to the number of donuts, then make sure the height clears icing and toppings. A little extra space keeps donuts in shape.

### Pie boxes

Pies should fit snugly without sliding. For decorative crusts or whipped toppings, choose a slightly taller box so nothing touches the lid.

## Tips for Accurate Measurements

- Measure your product after adding frosting, toppings and decorations.
- Always record dimensions as L × W × H.
- Allow 1–2 inches of extra space for decorations and easy placement.
- Use inside dimensions for the most accurate fit.
- Double-check before you place your order.

## Need Help With Sizing?

Our in-house team can work out your bakery box dimensions for you, and our design support is free. Order [custom bakery boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/bakery-boxes/) at wholesale prices with free shipping, or [get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

# Measure Your Box Dimensions: A Comprehensive Guide

Length, width, depth: the right order to measure a box and the allowances to add for a snug fit.

By Sarah AshleyMarch 3, 2025

![Measure Your Box Dimensions: A Comprehensive Guide](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/how-messure-a-box.webp)

Accurate measurements make sure your product fits its box perfectly. One mistake can throw off the box’s shape and design, and the dimensions also drive your choice of material, box style and even warehouse costs. Measuring looks simple, but there is more to it than you might think. This guide covers both the outside and inside dimensions of a box.

## Why Measurements Matter in Box Design

Dimensions decide how your box looks, which materials suit it and how much it costs to store. The box has to be made to the right size so your product fits securely and stays protected, so it pays to get the measurements right the first time.

## The Three Measurements You Need

- Length
- Width
- Height (depth)

All you need is a tape measure and a ruler.

Tip: round each measurement to the nearest whole inch. It keeps your numbers consistent and makes it easier to compare against standard box sizes.

## How to Measure the Outside of a Box

### Step 1: Length

Place the box on a flat surface and measure the longest side from left to right.

### Step 2: Width

Measure the shorter side from left to right.

### Step 3: Height

Stand the box upright and measure from top to bottom. Don’t include the flaps: length and width are measured on the panel with the flaps, but height is measured on a side wall without them.

## How to Measure the Inside of a Box

You need the same three measurements on the inside:

1. Open the box, and lay it flat if possible.
2. Length: place the tape along the bottom edge and measure the longest inside side.
3. Width: measure the shorter bottom side, from one inside wall to the other.
4. Depth: measure from the inside bottom to the top edge.

Tip: always record measurements in the order Length × Width × Depth. If you need inserts, leave extra room inside.

## Why Inside Dimensions Matter Most

The packaging industry works from inside dimensions, because outside measurements don’t account for the thickness of the material. Inside dimensions:

- Show the real usable space for your product.
- Account for the thickness of paperboard or corrugated board.
- Stop products from fitting too tightly or moving around.
- Give manufacturers what they need to make accurate boxes.

This is especially important for [corrugated mailer boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/corrugated-mailer-boxes/), where the fluted layer adds thickness to every wall. A box can look right from the outside but have less room inside than you expect.

## How to Calculate a Box’s Volume

Volume tells you how much space a box takes up when stacked in a warehouse. Multiply length × width × height. The result is in cubic units, such as cubic inches.

Packaging Ideas

# The Ultimate Packaging Design Checklist: Beyond the Basics

A checklist for artwork, bleed, colors, barcodes and finishes so your packaging design is print-ready first time.

By Sarah AshleyMarch 3, 2026

![The Ultimate Packaging Design Checklist: Beyond the Basics](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/the-ultimate-packaging-design.webp)

Packaging is the first story your product tells, the stage where your brand performs before anyone touches what is inside. In crowded aisles and online marketplaces, it can decide whether you are noticed or ignored. Done well, it protects, persuades and promotes; done poorly, it undermines trust. This checklist goes beyond the basics, from life cycle assessments to dimensional weight, so your packaging strategy leads rather than follows.

## 1. Define the Purpose

Purpose anchors every design decision:

- Protection: fragile goods need cushioning and durability.
- Presentation: luxury items need elegance and premium finishes.
- Efficiency: e-commerce packaging must be compact and frustration-free.
- Experience: subscription boxes should delight on opening.

## 2. Know Your Audience

- Gen Z: bold colors, eco credentials, QR codes.
- Millennials: minimalism, authenticity, shareable design.
- Luxury buyers: matte finishes, embossing, tactile details.
- Online shoppers: compact, resealable, easy-open designs.

## 3. Make Sustainability Credible

Buyers want proof, not just claims. Consider FSC-certified paper, recycling icons, lightweight materials like kraft and paperboard, and compostable films such as PLA. A life cycle assessment (LCA) tracks energy, emissions and waste from production to disposal, so you can show measurable progress.

## 4. Check Compliance and Standards

- ISO 18601 for packaging and the environment
- FDA rules for food and cosmetics labeling
- Marketplace packaging requirements for e-commerce
- Hazmat rules for chemicals and dangerous goods

## 5. Use Color Psychology

- Red: urgency, appetite, excitement
- Blue: trust, calm, professionalism
- Green: eco-friendliness, health
- Black: luxury, exclusivity

## 6. Choose Typography That Works

Serif fonts suggest tradition and reliability, sans-serif feels modern and clean, and script feels elegant and creative. Whatever you choose, it must stay legible, even in tiny online thumbnails.

## 7. Consider Shape and Ergonomics

- Easy-grip shapes: contours and textures help with bottles of drinks, cleaning products and cosmetics.
- Resealable pouches: zip or press seals on [mylar bags](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-mylar-bags/) extend shelf life and encourage reuse.
- Flat-pack boxes: [tray and sleeve boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/tray-sleeve-boxes/), tab-lock mailers and [folding cartons](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/folding-cartons/) save warehouse and shipping space.
- Stackability: boxes like [rigid drawer boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/rigid-drawer-boxes/) and [magnetic closure boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/magnetic-closure-boxes/) stack and stand neatly on shelves.

## 8. Get the Size Right

Too small risks damage; too big wastes material and money.

- Standard sizes: many categories have common dimensions. Bakery boxes, for example, are often around 6 × 6 × 3″ for cupcakes and 10 × 10 × 5″ for cakes. See [bakery box sizes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/measure-your-bakery-box-dimensions/).
- Custom sizes: for unique products, a perfect fit reduces movement and damage and looks polished.
- Volume: minimize air gaps to cut dimensional (DIM) weight charges and material.
- Convenience: right-sized boxes are easier to carry, store and reuse.

Learn how in [measure your box dimensions](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/measure-your-box-dimensions/).

## 9. Pick the Right Printing Method

- Digital: short runs, prototypes and variable data like QR codes.
- Offset: large volumes with sharp, consistent color and lower unit cost.
- Flexography: corrugated boxes and flexible packaging.
- Rotogravure: photo-quality printing for films and premium packaging.
- Screen printing: bold, opaque colors on specialty materials.

## 10. Apply Finishes and Effects

- Matte or gloss: subtle sophistication or vivid shine.
- [Foil stamping](/blog/what-is-foil-stamping/): metallic logos for luxury branding.
- [Embossing](/blog/what-is-embossing/) and [debossing](/blog/what-is-debossing/): tactile depth.
- [Spot UV](/blog/what-is-spot-uv/): selective gloss for contrast and focus.
- Soft-touch: a velvety, premium feel.
- Holographic and metallic: eye-catching effects that appeal to younger audiences.

## 11. Design the Unboxing

Unboxing videos are watched by millions, and a satisfying reveal builds loyalty and reorders.

- Surprise: inserts, hidden compartments and layered reveals make subscriptions something to look forward to.
- Tissue, ribbons and inserts: tactile details that signal care and exclusivity.
- QR codes and NFC: connect the physical box to your online community.

## 12. Tell a Story

- Heritage: design cues that convey your history build authenticity.
- Sustainability: share eco milestones and certifications transparently.
- Origin stories: inserts or QR codes explaining where ingredients come from.

People remember stories longer than features.

## 13. Add Smart Technology

- NFC tags to verify authenticity
- QR codes for supply chain traceability
- AR experiences that engage buyers

## 14. Get the Information Hierarchy Right

Shoppers scan packaging in seconds, so design for speed: product name → benefits → legal text. Include ingredients and compliance information, and use icons to simplify.

## 15. Plan for Logistics and Storage

- Stackable boxes that save space
- Moisture-resistant materials
- Strategic barcode placement
- Resealable, return-friendly designs

## 16. Measure Cost Against Value

- Damage destroys trust: customers blame your brand, not the courier.
- Excess packaging raises costs and frustrates eco-conscious buyers.
- Smart design balances cost and value.
- Total cost of ownership: include production, shipping, returns and disposal.

See [how much does packaging cost?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/how-much-does-packaging-cost/)

## 17. Test and Prototype

- Drop tests to simulate shipping impacts.
- Climate and shelf-life tests for food, pharma and frozen goods.
- Focus groups for feedback on usability, looks and messaging.
- Material prototypes to compare corrugated, rigid and kraft on cost, sustainability and performance. Try our [sample kits](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/sample-kits/).

## 18. Optimize for Retail and E-Commerce

| Aspect | Retail packaging | E-commerce packaging |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main goal | Win attention on the shelf | Survive shipping and read well in thumbnails |
| Design focus | Bold color, clear type, shelf appeal | Compact size, clarity at small scale |
| Compliance | Barcodes, nutrition facts, legal labels | Marketplace rules, DIM weight |
| Experience | Easy to carry, visually appealing | Easy to open, reseal and return |
| Logistics | Stackable, display-ready | Shipping efficiency, lower DIM costs |
| Marketing role | Impulse buys, brand story | Reviews, repeat orders, search ranking |

For retail, [shelf-ready packaging](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-shelf-ready-packaging/) helps you earn better placement, and scannable barcodes and accurate labels prevent rejections. Online, frustration-free, compact packaging lowers shipping fees and can help visibility on major marketplaces.

## 19. Measure Results

- Sales lift after a redesign
- Reviews that mention packaging
- Return rates, where fewer damages mean savings
- Customer sentiment about the packaging itself, via surveys

## Final Checklist

- ☐ Purpose defined
- ☐ Audience understood
- ☐ Sustainability integrated
- ☐ Compliance checked
- ☐ Color and type psychology applied
- ☐ Box size selected
- ☐ Shape and ergonomics optimized
- ☐ Printing method chosen
- ☐ Finishes applied
- ☐ Unboxing designed
- ☐ Smart technology considered
- ☐ Logistics streamlined
- ☐ Retail and e-commerce needs balanced
- ☐ Testing and prototyping complete

## Closing Thoughts

Packaging isn’t a passive container. It shapes perception, drives sales and builds loyalty. Work through this checklist and your packaging becomes a growth engine, not a cost center. Need help? Our design support is free: [get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

## FAQs

### Why is packaging design so important?

It is your product’s first impression: it protects, attracts buyers and communicates your values.

### How is retail packaging different from e-commerce packaging?

Retail focuses on shelf appeal and compliance; e-commerce focuses on shipping efficiency, durability and easy returns.

### How do I know a design works?

Test it with drop and climate trials and focus groups, then track returns, reviews and sales after launch.

### Which metrics measure packaging success?

Sales lift, reviews mentioning packaging, return rates and customer sentiment about the packaging.

Informative

# Paper Weight Chart With Conversion Calculator

Convert between GSM, pounds and points with a simple chart, and see which weights suit which box types.

By Sarah AshleyApril 1, 2026

![Paper Weight Chart With Conversion Calculator](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/paper-weight-chart-with-conversion-calculator.webp)

Paper weight can be confusing, especially when suppliers use different units. This guide explains the three units packaging manufacturers use for weight and thickness (PT, LBS and GSM) and gives conversion charts for the most common paper stocks.

## What Is PT?

PT means points, a unit of paper thickness (caliper) used mainly in North America. One point equals 1/1000 of an inch (0.001″), so 10 pt board is 0.010″ thick and 16 pt is 0.016″. The higher the number, the thicker and stiffer the board.

## What Is LBS?

LBS means pounds and describes the weight of paper used for packaging, newspapers, flyers and more. Heavier generally means thicker, but it depends on the paper grade: 60 lb text paper is much lighter and thinner than 60 lb cover paper, because the two are weighed on different base sheet sizes.

## What Is GSM?

GSM means grams per square meter, the international standard for paper weight. Higher numbers mean heavier, thicker paper. Everyday paper is around 80–100 GSM, while 300 GSM and above is heavy cardstock.

## Common Paper Types

- Text stock
- Uncoated stock
- Coated stock

## Text Stock Weight Chart

Text stock is a light paper used for books, magazines, flyers and brochures. It is usually specified in PT or GSM.

| Text stock (PT) | Approx. GSM |
| --- | --- |
| 10 pt | ~60 |
| 12 pt | ~72 |
| 14 pt | ~84 |
| 16 pt | ~96 |
| 18 pt | ~108 |

There is no exact formula, but this gives a close estimate: GSM ≈ PT × 600 ÷ 100. For example, 24 pt text stock ≈ 24 × 600 ÷ 100 ≈ 144 GSM.

## Uncoated Stock Weight Chart

Uncoated stock is used for boxes, business cards and more. It is much more durable than text stock and prints packaging designs well. It is usually specified in PT.

| Uncoated stock (PT) | Approx. GSM |
| --- | --- |
| 10 pt | ~140 |
| 12 pt | ~168 |
| 14 pt | ~196 |
| 16 pt | ~224 |
| 18 pt | ~252 |

Because it is thicker, the multiplier is higher: GSM ≈ PT × 1400 ÷ 100. For example, 20 pt ≈ 280 GSM.

## Coated Stock Weight Charts

Coated stock is the heaviest and most durable option. It comes as C1S (coated one side) and C2S (coated both sides).

### C1S

| C1S stock (PT) | Approx. GSM |
| --- | --- |
| 10 pt | ~150 |
| 12 pt | ~180 |
| 14 pt | ~210 |
| 16 pt | ~240 |
| 18 pt | ~270 |

Add a coating adjustment (C) of 100: GSM ≈ PT × (1400 + C) ÷ 100. For 20 pt: 20 × 1500 ÷ 100 ≈ 300 GSM.

### C2S

| C2S stock (PT) | Approx. GSM |
| --- | --- |
| 10 pt | ~165 |
| 12 pt | ~198 |
| 14 pt | ~231 |
| 16 pt | ~264 |
| 18 pt | ~297 |

Add two coating adjustments, a medium one of 100 and a high one of 150: GSM ≈ PT × (1400 + C₁ + C₂) ÷ 100. For 20 pt: 20 × 1650 ÷ 100 ≈ 330 GSM.

## How to Convert LBS to GSM

Converting pounds is simpler:

- Text stock: GSM ≈ lbs × 1.48
- Coated stock: GSM ≈ lbs × 2.71

| Weight (lbs) | Text stock (GSM) | Coated stock (GSM) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 54 lbs | ~80 | ~146 |
| 61 lbs | ~90 | ~165 |
| 68 lbs | ~100 | ~184 |
| 82 lbs | ~121 | ~222 |
| 101 lbs | ~150 | ~274 |

Note: all values are approximate and may differ slightly from GSM measured by weighing a sample.

Not sure which weight your box needs? Ask our team through [contact us](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/contact-us/), or see our [materials guide](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/materials/).

pages.content_markdown:
Box Types

# Retail Boxes vs Corrugated Boxes: What’s the Difference and Which One Is Right for Your Product?

Retail boxes sell on the shelf; corrugated boxes protect in transit. Compare materials, strength and branding, and see why many brands use both.

By Sarah AshleyNovember 16, 2026

![Retail Boxes vs Corrugated Boxes: What’s the Difference and Which One Is Right for Your Product?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-rigid-boxes-vs-custom-corrugated.webp)

Packaging decisions often start with materials. Paperboard or corrugated? Lightweight or heavy-duty? Looks or protection? Those questions matter, but they miss the bigger point: packaging exists to help your product succeed.

Sometimes success means standing out on a crowded shelf. Sometimes it means surviving a long shipping journey. Often it means both. Retail boxes and corrugated boxes can look similar to a buyer, but they play very different roles. Here is how they differ and how to choose.

## What Are Retail Boxes?

Retail boxes are usually described as display packaging, but their real job is to remove doubt from the buyer’s mind. Before buying, shoppers wonder:

- Can I trust this product?
- Is it worth the price?
- Will it do what it promises?
- Does this brand look professional?

A good retail box answers those questions before the product is ever used, through its design, structure, messaging and feel. For example:

- A luxury cosmetic box might use soft-touch lamination for a premium feel.
- A supplement box might highlight certifications and ingredients.
- A tech product might use a minimal design that signals simplicity and innovation.

When packaging looks premium, customers tend to assume the product is too. Retail boxes don’t just hold products; they set expectations.

In short: retail boxes are what customers buy from. Examples include makeup, perfume, soap and candle boxes. See our [retail boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/retail-boxes/).

## What Are Corrugated Boxes?

Corrugated boxes are a form of risk management. The fluted layer inside the board creates small air pockets that absorb pressure and spread out impact, which makes corrugated packaging especially effective when shipping conditions are unpredictable.

It also brings operational benefits: warehouses can stack products more efficiently, fewer goods are lost or damaged, e-commerce brands ship with more confidence, and retailers move stock through distribution with fewer losses.

In short: corrugated boxes are what your products ship in. Examples include mailer boxes, shipping cartons, subscription boxes and warehouse cartons. See our [corrugated boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/corrugated-boxes/).

## The Materials Behind the Difference

### Retail boxes rely on dense board

Most retail boxes are made from paperboard with a dense fiber structure, which allows crisp folds, detailed printing, smooth finishes and clean edges. Luxury products often use rigid stock, which gets its strength from density rather than structure.

### Corrugated boxes rely on structure

Corrugated board gets its strength from the flutes, which act like tiny support columns. They provide:

- Shock absorption
- Compression resistance
- Better stacking strength
- Cushioning

Much of that strength comes from geometry rather than thickness, which is why corrugated boxes stay light while carrying heavy loads.

## Shelf Appeal vs Supply Chain Performance

Products compete in two very different places: at the point of sale and inside the supply chain.

### Retail boxes win on the shelf

A retail box has only seconds to grab attention. It is judged on visual impact, color quality, typography, finishes and brand storytelling.

### Corrugated boxes win in logistics

Corrugated packaging is judged on drop performance, compression strength, durability in transit, warehouse efficiency and how well it protects the product.

So instead of asking which is better, ask where your product is most at risk:

- If visibility is the challenge, invest more in retail boxes.
- If damage is the challenge, corrugated boxes matter more.
- If both matter, combine the two.

## Retail Boxes Influence Buying Decisions

Shoppers like to think they buy rationally, but first impressions often come first and the reasoning follows. In a busy store, with hundreds of products competing for attention, customers rely on visual cues to decide quickly. Structure, color, finishes and typography all shape that impression before anyone reads a feature list.

- A premium-looking box signals confidence.
- A well-designed box suggests professionalism.
- A polished presentation lowers the perceived risk of buying.

That is why luxury brands invest in specialty finishes, rigid structures, foil stamping, embossing and premium coatings. They don’t change the product, but they change how its value is perceived.

## Corrugated Boxes Protect Your Reputation

Corrugated boxes protect more than products; they protect customer trust. When an order arrives damaged, the direct costs are obvious: replacements, customer service time and refunds. The hidden costs are often bigger:

- A customer who receives a damaged product is less likely to buy again.
- A negative review can put off future buyers.
- Your brand’s credibility can suffer.

By absorbing shock and spreading pressure, corrugated board helps products survive warehouses, sorting hubs and last-mile delivery. Every undamaged delivery builds trust, which is just as important as protecting the product itself.

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Feature | Retail Boxes | Corrugated Boxes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main purpose | Product presentation | Product protection |
| Material | Paperboard, cardstock, rigid stock | Corrugated fiberboard |
| Print quality | Excellent | Good to excellent |
| Strength | Moderate | High |
| Shelf appeal | Excellent | Moderate |
| Shipping performance | Limited | Excellent |
| Luxury finishes | Extensive | Limited |
| Weight | Light to moderate | Slightly heavier |
| Product protection | Basic | Advanced |

## Why This Decision Matters

Packaging used to have one main job: catch the eye on a shelf. Today a buyer might discover your product on social media, compare it online, watch an unboxing video and then receive it at home. Packaging now affects:

- First impressions and brand perception
- Purchase decisions and customer confidence
- Shipping performance and product protection
- Reviews and repeat purchases
- Operational efficiency and logistics costs

Focusing only on looks, or only on protection, tends to create hidden costs later: damaged goods, poor experiences, more returns or weaker shelf impact. The strongest brands choose [custom packaging](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-boxes/) that supports the whole journey.

## Why Many Brands Need Both

A product passes through several stages before and after it reaches the customer: discovery, evaluation, purchase, delivery, unboxing and retention. Each stage asks something different of the packaging.

Retail boxes shine during discovery and evaluation, where they attract attention, share product information and help shoppers compare. Corrugated boxes shine during delivery and fulfillment, keeping the product intact in storage and transit. They aren’t competitors; they solve different problems at different stages.

## The Best Strategy: Layered Packaging

Customers want products that look premium and arrive safely. A retail box inside a protective corrugated shipper does both: the retail box delivers presentation, and the corrugated box delivers protection. This layered approach is increasingly common in beauty, electronics, food, wellness and subscription businesses.

## Final Thoughts

Neither box is better overall. Retail boxes shape perception, communicate value and win attention. Corrugated boxes preserve quality, prevent damage and protect trust. For your next project, ask which part of the customer journey needs the most support, and the right packaging usually follows.

## FAQs

### What is the main difference between retail and corrugated boxes?

Retail boxes are designed for presentation and branding. Corrugated boxes are designed for protection, storage and shipping.

### Are retail boxes strong enough for shipping?

They can handle light products, but they aren’t ideal for shipping on their own. Most brands ship them inside corrugated boxes.

### Which is better for e-commerce?

Corrugated boxes are usually preferred for e-commerce because they offer better cushioning, durability and shipping performance.

### Can I use both together?

Yes. Many brands use retail boxes for shelf appeal and branding, then ship them inside corrugated boxes for protection. [Get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/) for both.

# Rigid Boxes vs Folding Cartons vs Corrugated: Which Packaging Should You Choose?

A side-by-side comparison of the three main packaging families by cost, strength, look and best use.

By Sarah AshleyDecember 15, 2025

![Rigid Boxes vs Folding Cartons vs Corrugated: Which Packaging Should You Choose?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-rigid-boxes-vs-custom-corrugated.webp)

One of the first questions brands ask before a launch is which packaging to choose. Your box is your first touchpoint with the customer, and three options come up again and again: rigid boxes, folding cartons and corrugated boxes. You want your product to look premium, stay protected, ship safely and still make financial sense. Here is a practical comparison.

## 1. Rigid Boxes

Think of a smartphone box, a designer perfume box or a luxury gift box: solid, non-collapsing, built from thick board and wrapped in printed or textured paper.

- Very strong and durable
- Premium, luxurious look
- Used for high-value products
- Not shipped flat, so they take more storage

Best for: electronics, luxury cosmetics, jewelry, premium gifts and subscription boxes with a “wow” unboxing. See [rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/).

## 2. Folding Cartons

The printed paperboard boxes used for cereal, skincare, small gadgets, snacks and medicine. They ship flat and fold into shape at packing.

- Light and cost-effective
- Excellent print quality
- Ship flat, saving space and freight
- Less sturdy than rigid or corrugated

Best for: food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, light retail products and shelf packaging. See [folding cartons](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/folding-cartons/).

## 3. Corrugated Boxes

Best known as the brown boxes online orders arrive in, though they can be fully printed. A wavy fluted layer between two liners gives them strength.

- Very strong and impact-resistant
- Built for shipping and logistics
- Single wall, double wall and more
- Can be printed and branded

Best for: mailers, e-commerce, heavy or fragile items, bulk packaging and long-distance subscriptions. See [corrugated boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/corrugated-boxes/).

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Feature | Rigid boxes | Folding cartons | Corrugated boxes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Strength | High | Low to medium | Medium to high |
| Look and feel | Premium, luxury | Clean, retail-ready | Practical to premium |
| Cost per unit | High | Low | Medium |
| Best use | Luxury and gift products | Light retail items | Shipping, heavy or fragile items |
| Storage and shipping | Bulky, don’t fold flat | Very space-efficient | Space-efficient, ship flat |
| Inserts | Excellent (foam, EVA, paperboard, pulp) | Good (paperboard inserts) | Excellent (corrugated inserts, partitions) |
| Environmental impact | Can be eco-friendly; more material | Highly eco-friendly; less material | Usually recyclable; more material than cartons |
| Branding | Premium wraps, specialty finishes | Excellent print | Good to excellent |
| Premium features | Magnets, ribbons, textures, foil, embossing | Spot UV, foil | Handles, structural add-ons, quality print |

## When to Choose Rigid Boxes

- You sell a premium product, like a high-end skincare set, luxury chocolates or tech accessories, where buyers expect a special experience.
- Unboxing is part of your marketing, through influencers, social media or gifting.
- Your product needs structured protection, such as sets, delicate bottles or multi-part products with inserts.
- You want the box to be kept, for jewelry, keepsakes and storage, keeping your brand in customers’ homes.

Downsides: the highest cost, more warehouse space, and heavier, bulkier shipping. Choose rigid when your price and positioning justify it. Learn more: [What is a rigid box?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-a-rigid-box/)

## When to Choose Folding Cartons

- You need attractive, affordable retail packaging for face creams, protein bars, tea or over-the-counter medicine, with plenty of space for design and information.
- Your product isn’t very fragile or heavy.
- You want low shipping and storage costs, since flat cartons save space at volume.
- Sustainability matters: paperboard with recycled or FSC-certified content uses less material.

Downsides: they don’t feel quite as luxurious as rigid boxes, even with good finishes, and usually need a corrugated shipper for transit.

## When to Choose Corrugated Boxes

- You ship direct to customers, such as clothes, books, home décor or kits. Use single wall for light items and double wall for more protection.
- Protection matters more than luxury, though custom print and inserts make them presentable.
- You want one box to do everything, like printed subscription boxes that work as shipper and presentation.
- You sell larger or heavier items, such as electronics, appliances, bulk food and multipacks.

Downsides: bulkier once assembled, not naturally luxurious, and more material than cartons, though usually recyclable. Learn more in our [guide to corrugated boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/guide-to-corrugated-boxes/).

## Key Questions to Ask

### What is your product’s price and perceived value?

Luxury products suit rigid boxes; everyday products suit folding cartons; wide price ranges or heavy shipping suit corrugated, or corrugated with cartons inside.

### How fragile is it?

Very delicate items such as glass or electronics need corrugated with inserts; premium fragile items can use rigid boxes; robust products are fine in a carton or corrugated box.

### Where is the first impression?

On a shelf, cartons or rigid boxes both work. Online, a printed corrugated mailer is usually best, with a rigid box or carton inside for the unboxing.

### What are your budget and volumes?

High volumes on a budget suit cartons or basic corrugated; smaller premium runs suit rigid; growing brands often combine corrugated for shipping with cartons for retail.

## Final Thoughts

No option is universally better. The right choice depends on your product’s value and fragility, where it is sold, your budget and positioning, and the experience you want to create. Often the smartest answer is a combination, such as a carton or rigid box inside a protective corrugated shipper. # 7 Creative Small Business Packaging Ideas

Seven affordable ways small brands can make their packaging memorable without big minimums or big budgets.

By Sarah AshleySeptember 17, 2026

![7 Creative Small Business Packaging Ideas](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/creative-packaging-ideas.webp)

Small businesses work hard to win new customers and even harder to keep them coming back. One of the simplest ways to stand out is creative packaging that presents your product well and catches attention in an instant. Here are seven packaging ideas to help a small business boost sales and presentation.

## Why Packaging Matters for Small Businesses

Packaging protects products in storage and shipping and makes the first impression. Good packaging makes your products look professional, improves brand recognition and creates a better unboxing. It also gives you space for your logo, colors and product details. With the right [custom packaging](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-boxes/), small brands build trust, earn repeat orders and compete confidently with bigger names.

Mix, match and adapt the ideas below to suit your brand and products.

## 1. Corrugated Boxes

Many small businesses start out selling online through marketplaces and their own stores, which keeps warehouse costs down. Making a lasting impression still matters, and custom [corrugated boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/corrugated-boxes/) protect shipments while showing off your brand. Popular styles:

- [Mailer boxes](/mailer-boxes/): ship e-commerce orders safely and deliver a great unboxing, printed with your logo and key information.
- Roll end tuck top boxes: a sturdy corrugated build with a tuck-top lid and plenty of printable space.
- Roll end tuck front boxes: a front-locking tuck closure for extra security and a professional unboxing.

## 2. Paperboard Boxes

Paperboard boxes, or [folding cartons](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/folding-cartons/), are light, affordable and highly customizable. They suit retail goods, cosmetics, food, candles and soaps, and their smooth surface prints beautifully. Popular styles:

- Reverse tuck end boxes: simple, versatile boxes for cosmetics, soaps, medicines and small retail items.
- Sleeve boxes: an outer sleeve slides over the product or an inner tray for a clean look and extra print space.
- Window boxes: a clear window shows the product without opening the pack, great for bakery, cosmetics and gifts.

## 3. Rigid Boxes

For luxury goods, gifts, jewelry, cosmetics and high-value items, [rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/) made from thick chipboard feel strong and premium, and support finishes, inserts and print. Popular styles:

- Two-piece boxes: a separate lid and base for a classic premium look.
- Magnetic closure boxes: hidden magnets keep the box shut and make opening feel special.
- Drawer boxes: a sliding tray inside a sleeve, popular for jewelry, watches, cosmetics and electronics.

## 4. Plastic Mailers and Poly Bags

If you ship clothing, accessories or other soft goods, lightweight plastic mailers cut shipping costs and protect against dust, moisture and dirt:

- Poly mailers for clothing, textiles and non-fragile items.
- Bubble mailers with cushioned lining for small electronics, accessories and cosmetics.
- Custom printed poly bags carrying your logo, colors and patterns.

## 5. Paper Mailers

Paper mailers are simple, light and printable, ideal for documents, books, apparel and accessories:

- Kraft mailers for light products, documents and small accessories.
- Padded paper mailers with internal cushioning for delicate items without bulk.
- Expandable paper mailers with gussets for products of different sizes or thicknesses.

## 6. Custom Tape and Stickers

You don’t always need fully printed boxes. Branded tape and stickers are an affordable way to brand plain boxes, bags and mailers:

- Custom packing tape printed with your logo, name or pattern.
- Logo stickers on plain boxes, bags or tissue paper.
- Thank-you stickers that make every order feel personal.

## 7. Custom Tissue Paper

Tissue paper adds a layer of presentation inside boxes and bags, wraps and protects products, and makes unboxing feel premium for very little cost:

- Logo-printed tissue with a repeating brand pattern.
- Colored tissue in brand or seasonal colors.
- Tissue sealed with a sticker for a simple, professional finish.

## Final Takeaways

Creative packaging protects your products and builds a stronger brand, and it doesn’t have to be expensive. Even stickers, printed tape, tissue or branded mailers can make your packaging feel professional. Choose based on your product, shipping needs, budget and brand goals.

With no minimum order, Pack Legacy is built for small businesses. [Get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

Box Types

# Different Types of Boxes in the Packaging Industry

A visual tour of the main box types, from tuck end cartons and mailers to rigid, display and specialty boxes.

By Sarah AshleyAugust 4, 2026

![Different Types of Boxes in the Packaging Industry](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/types-of-boxes-in-the-packaging.webp)

Boxes are part of everyday life. Every time we shop, the packaging that catches our eye plays a part in what we buy. Custom boxes are designed to do exactly that: attract customers, drive sales and build a connection with the brand. Here are the main types of boxes in the packaging industry and the styles within each.

## The Three Main Types of Boxes

- [Folding cartons](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/folding-cartons/)
- [Rigid boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/)
- [Corrugated boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/corrugated-boxes/)

## Folding Cartons

Folding cartons, also called paperboard cartons or boxes, are the most common box type. They are made from thin, light but durable paperboard, and you see them everywhere in retail, from cereal boxes to lipstick and cookie boxes. The five main styles are:

### Straight tuck end boxes

Top and bottom flaps tuck in the same direction for a clean look and quick assembly. Common for cosmetics, electronics, pharmaceuticals and other light retail products.

### Reverse tuck end boxes

Flaps fold in opposite directions, which reduces paper waste while staying secure. Widely used for food, cosmetics, supplements and everyday goods.

### Auto lock bottom boxes

A pre-glued base locks automatically when the box is opened, saving assembly time and adding strength for heavier products such as candles, beverages and skincare.

### 1-2-3 lock bottom boxes

Interlocking bottom flaps form a strong base without glue, supporting medium to heavy products cost-effectively. Common for food, electronics and retail goods.

### Seal end boxes

Top and bottom flaps are permanently sealed for maximum protection and tamper resistance. Used for pharmaceuticals, frozen foods and healthcare products.

## Rigid Boxes

Rigid boxes, also called setup boxes, are the luxury option. They are made from durable [rigid stock](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-rigid-stock/) wrapped in printed paper for a refined finish. Six styles are especially popular:

### Magnetic closure boxes

Hidden magnets give a secure, premium close and a memorable unboxing. Popular for luxury gifts, cosmetics, jewelry and electronics. See [magnetic closure boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/magnetic-closure-boxes/).

### Collapsible boxes

Fold flat when not in use to save storage and shipping space, while keeping a premium look. Used for apparel, gifts and subscription boxes.

### Two-piece boxes

A separate lid and base that fit snugly together, with sturdy protection and premium presentation for chocolates, apparel, electronics and gifts.

### Shoulder neck boxes

A raised inner neck between base and lid creates a layered, premium look and added strength. Popular for perfume, watches, jewelry and cosmetics.

### Drawer boxes

An inner tray slides out of an outer sleeve for an elegant reveal. Used for cosmetics, jewelry, electronics, chocolates and gifts.

### Book-style boxes

A hinged lid opens like a hardcover book, often with a magnetic catch. Used for premium gifts, electronics, cosmetics and corporate packaging.

## Corrugated Boxes

Corrugated boxes are among the strongest packaging options. Corrugated board has a fluted layer between two flat liners, giving excellent strength, cushioning and protection in shipping and storage, which makes it the standard for shipping boxes, moving boxes and e-commerce mailers. The five main styles are:

### Mailer boxes

Self-locking boxes that protect products without extra packing and look good doing it. Ideal for e-commerce, subscriptions, PR kits, apparel and cosmetics. See [mailer boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/mailer-boxes/).

### Regular slotted containers (RSC)

The most widely used shipping box: simple, strong, easy to assemble and cost-effective for shipping, storage and industrial use.

### Full overlap slotted containers (FOL)

Flaps overlap fully when closed for extra cushioning and stacking strength. Used for heavy or fragile items such as equipment, glass and auto parts.

### Half slotted containers (HSC)

One open side with flaps on the bottom, often paired with a separate lid. Used for storage, display, shipping and warehouse organization.

### Roll end tuck top boxes (RETT)

Rolled side panels and a tuck-in lid lock securely and protect products in transit. Popular for subscriptions, cosmetics, electronics and e-commerce.

## Final Takeaways

The right box protects your product, strengthens your brand and creates a better customer experience. Folding cartons, rigid boxes and corrugated boxes each serve different needs, and knowing their styles helps you choose packaging that works and looks right.

Compare every style on our [box by style](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/box-by-style/) page, or [get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/).

# Types of Packaging: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary

The three levels of packaging and the job each one does, from the product itself to the pallet.

By Sarah AshleyJuly 1, 2025

![Types of Packaging: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/types-of-packaging-primary-secondary-and-tertiary.webp)

Packaging is far more than a container. In a competitive market it can lift your product’s value and your brand’s image, or hold them back, so it pays to know which kind you need. By function, there are three main types: primary, secondary and tertiary.

## The 3 Main Types of Packaging

Packaging can be made from glass, plastic, cardboard, wood and more, but by what it does, every package falls into one of three levels.

## Primary Packaging

Primary packaging touches the product directly. It is the first layer around the product, and its job is to protect it and keep it in the best condition. It is also the first thing customers see when they handle your product, especially in e-commerce, so it should look good and carry key information such as ingredients and instructions.

### Examples of primary packaging

- Bottles and jars for drinks, shampoos and oils.
- Boxes for electronics like phones and cameras, and foods like [cereal](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/cereal-boxes/) and [chocolate](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/chocolate-boxes/).
- Wrappers for candy bars, chips and snacks.
- Blister packs for medicines and toys, though many pharmaceutical brands use [medicine boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/medicine-boxes/).
- Tins and cans for food and beverages.
- Pouches for snacks, coffee and more.
- Tubes for toothpaste, creams and gels.

## Secondary Packaging

Secondary packaging is the layer around the primary packaging. It adds protection in storage and transport, groups products together, and gives you a large surface for branding and artwork.

### Examples of secondary packaging

- Boxes and cartons: a box holding six juice bottles, or several macarons in [macaron boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/product/macaron-boxes/). Cartons suit heavier products.
- Trays: cardboard or plastic trays for beverages, tins and yogurt cups.
- Shipping and mailer boxes: the go-to choice for e-commerce. For direct-to-consumer brands they should look as good as they protect. See [mailer boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/mailer-boxes/).

## Tertiary Packaging

Tertiary packaging is used to move products in bulk, for example to a store. It encloses the primary and secondary packaging, groups many units into one load, and is built for durability in transit. Common examples are wooden pallets, plastic pallets and wooden crates.

## Why Knowing the Types Matters

With so many similar products on the market, packaging is often what sets yours apart and creates a positive, memorable impression. Understanding the three levels helps you choose the right solution for your product and what you need the packaging to do. You wouldn’t pack a T-shirt in a glass bottle, and a box can’t be the primary packaging for wine.

- Primary packaging preserves your product’s quality and carries your brand.
- Secondary packaging adds protection in transit.
- Tertiary packaging makes handling, storage and transport of bulk loads safe and efficient.

Your brand message doesn’t have to appear on all three, but keep the look consistent across them.

## Wrapping Up

Knowing the difference between primary, secondary and tertiary packaging helps you decide exactly what your products need. For high-quality [custom packaging](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-boxes/), [get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/) from Pack Legacy.

## FAQs

### What is primary packaging?

Packaging in direct contact with the product, which protects it and keeps it in good condition.

### What is secondary packaging?

The layer around the primary packaging, adding protection for transport and storage.

### What is tertiary packaging?

Bulk packaging that holds primary and secondary packaging for safe shipping and handling.

### Why should primary packaging look appealing?

It is the first thing customers see when they interact with your product.

### What is the best secondary packaging for e-commerce?

Shipping boxes and mailer boxes.

### What are examples of tertiary packaging?

Wooden pallets, plastic pallets and wooden crates.

# What Is a Rigid Box?

Rigid boxes explained: how they are built, the main styles and why luxury brands rely on them.

By Sarah AshleyDecember 8, 2025

![What Is a Rigid Box?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-rigid-boxes.webp)

Think of the last time a box impressed you before you even saw the product: thick matte board, a weighty lid, crisp edges. That feeling is the magic of a rigid box, and a reminder that packaging is part of the product experience.

Rigid boxes are the go-to choice for luxury packaging. They are made from high-density paperboard two to four times thicker than standard board, which is why electronics, cosmetics, perfume, jewelry, gourmet food and high-end gifts so often come in them. Here is what makes them special, how they are made and why brands choose them.

## Key Features of Rigid Boxes

- Sturdy: chipboard and greyboard protect fragile items without bending or collapsing.
- Premium look: clean edges, smooth wraps and finishes like matte or gloss lamination, Spot UV, aqueous coating, varnish, embossing, debossing and foil.
- Solid structure: they don’t fold flat (except collapsible versions), which allows magnetic lids, drawers, clamshells and book-style openings, plus fabric linings, EVA foam, dividers or raised platforms inside.
- Memorable unboxing: the slow lift of a lid, the click of a magnet, the slide of a drawer.

## How Rigid Boxes Are Made

1. Design: dimensions, style, product fit, board thickness and branding placement are planned.
2. Cutting: sheets of [rigid stock](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-rigid-stock/) (chipboard, greyboard or recycled board) are die-cut into panels with millimeter accuracy.
3. Scoring and V-grooving: grooves along the fold lines let thick board bend cleanly, giving sharp corners.
4. Forming and gluing: panels are folded and joined, with corners reinforced to prevent splitting.
5. Wrapping: printed paper, textured stock, leatherette, fabric or recycled sheets are bonded seamlessly to the board.
6. Functional parts: magnets, ribbons, pull tabs and foam or molded inserts are added as needed.
7. Finishing: foil, embossing, Spot UV and interior printing, then a final quality check.

## Rigid Boxes vs Folding Cartons vs Corrugated

- Durability: fragile items like perfume, watches and electronics stay safe without extra packaging.
- Luxury perception: even a simple product feels more valuable.
- Unboxing: anticipation and emotion that customers remember.
- Customization: materials, finishes, inserts and accessories tailored to any brand style.

Rigid boxes can be eco-friendly too. Think of the last time a box impressed you before you even saw the product: thick matte board, a weighty lid, crisp edges. That feeling is the magic of a rigid box, and a reminder that packaging is part of the product experience.

Rigid boxes are the go-to choice for luxury packaging. They are made from high-density paperboard two to four times thicker than standard board, which is why electronics, cosmetics, perfume, jewelry, gourmet food and high-end gifts so often come in them. sections.content:
- Sturdy: chipboard and greyboard protect fragile items without bending or collapsing.
- Premium look: clean edges, smooth wraps and finishes like matte or gloss lamination, Spot UV, aqueous coating, varnish, embossing, debossing and foil.
- Solid structure: they don’t fold flat (except collapsible versions), which allows magnetic lids, drawers, clamshells and book-style openings, plus fabric linings, EVA foam, dividers or raised platforms inside.
- Memorable unboxing: the slow lift of a lid, the click of a magnet, the slide of a drawer.

sections.content:

4. Forming and gluing: panels are folded and joined, with corners reinforced to prevent splitting.
5. Wrapping: printed paper, textured stock, leatherette, fabric or recycled sheets are bonded seamlessly to the board.
6. Functional parts: magnets, ribbons, pull tabs and foam or molded inserts are added as needed.
7. Finishing: foil, embossing, Spot UV and interior printing, then a final quality check.

# What is CBD Packaging? A Complete Guide to CBD Packaging

What CBD packaging needs to do, the box styles brands use for oils, gummies and creams, and how to keep it compliant.

By Sarah AshleySeptember 11, 2026

![What is CBD Packaging? A Complete Guide to CBD Packaging](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/cbd-packaging.webp)

Demand for CBD products keeps growing, and so do CBD brands. But you can’t simply put a CBD product on a shelf; it needs packaging designed to protect it, inform customers and meet the rules.

CBD (cannabidiol) is a non-psychoactive compound from the cannabis plant. It is sold as tinctures, gummies, edibles, creams and more, and each format needs its own packaging. This guide covers the main types of CBD packaging, box styles and what to include in your design.

## What Is CBD Packaging?

CBD packaging is packaging made to store, transport and sell CBD products safely while complying with regulations. It can be customized in size, shape, style and material to suit oils, tinctures, edibles or topicals. Browse our [CBD boxes](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/cbd-boxes/).

## Types of CBD Packaging

- [Tincture boxes](/product/cbd-tincture-boxes/): hold oil bottles securely, with inserts for a snug fit and room for branding, dosage, ingredients and usage.
- [CBD gummies packaging](/product/cbd-gummies-boxes/): custom boxes or [mylar bags](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/custom-mylar-bags/) that keep edibles fresh, with space for flavor, dosage, ingredients and required labels.
- [CBD display boxes](/product/cbd-display-boxes/): organize several products at the counter for better visibility.
- [Pre-roll boxes](/product/cbd-pre-roll-packaging/): protect pre-rolls from crushing, moisture and contamination, with options for inserts and child-resistant features.
- Retail CBD boxes: protect products and improve shelf presentation in stores and dispensaries, with logos, instructions and warnings.
- Custom CBD boxes: fully tailored materials, sizes, print, finishes, inserts and styles.
- [E-liquid boxes](/product/e-liquid-boxes/): protect vape juice bottles, with flavor details, usage instructions and product information.

## CBD Box Styles and Their Uses

| Box style | Best for |
| --- | --- |
| Reverse tuck end | Tinctures, vape cartridges, oils, small bottles |
| Tray and sleeve | Gummies, tincture sets, pre-rolls, wellness kits |
| Two-piece | Tinctures and premium wellness products |
| Straight tuck end | Oils, tinctures, vape products, creams, capsules |
| Magnetic closure | Premium gift sets, tincture collections, gummies |
| Display box | Gummies, pre-rolls, cartridges, tinctures, small retail items |
| Mailer box | Shipping gummies, oils, tinctures, skincare, subscription kits |

- Reverse tuck end: opposite tuck flaps make it quick to assemble, and the compact build keeps light products secure.
- Tray and sleeve: a sliding sleeve creates a premium reveal, and the tray holds products and inserts securely.
- Two-piece: a separate lid and base for strong protection and luxury presentation.
- Straight tuck end: both flaps tuck the same way, leaving a clean front panel for branding and required information.
- Magnetic closure: a secure magnetic flap and a luxurious unboxing, with room for custom inserts.
- Display box: keeps multiple units organized and visible on counters and shelves.
- Mailer box: a sturdy build for shipping, with inserts to keep bottles and containers in place.

## What to Include When Designing CBD Packaging

CBD packaging must meet labeling rules, so plan space for:

- Product name and identity: say clearly what it is, such as CBD oil, cream, gummies or tincture.
- Net quantity: weight, volume or count, generally shown prominently on the main display panel.
- Ingredients: a complete list where required; cosmetics, for example, list ingredients in descending order of predominance.
- Manufacturer or distributor details: the business responsible for the product.
- Directions and warnings: usage, precautions and safety information, with enough room to stay readable.
- CBD labeling requirements: CBD content, batch information and any other federal or state requirements.
- State-specific rules: some states require cannabinoid content, QR codes, batch or testing details, or specific warnings. Always check the markets you sell in.

For more detail, read our [CBD packaging compliance guide](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/cbd-packaging-regulations/) and [CBD labeling requirements](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/cbd-labeling-requirements/).

## Where to Buy CBD Packaging

Choose a manufacturer that understands CBD labeling and compliance. Pack Legacy makes custom CBD boxes and keeps up to date with CBD regulations, so you can customize packaging to your needs while keeping products safe.

## Conclusion

CBD packaging protects products, supports your brand and helps you meet labeling requirements. Because CBD comes in so many forms, the right type, style, material and structure matter. Before finalizing, check protection, presentation, labeling and state rules. [Get a free quote](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/get-a-quote/) for your CBD packaging.

# What is Debossing?

Debossing presses a design into the board for a subtle, tactile look. Learn how it works and where it looks best.

By Sarah AshleyAugust 26, 2026

![What is Debossing?](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/debossing-blog.webp)

Debossing presses a design, logo, text or artwork into the surface of a material. Instead of raising it, debossing creates a recessed, sunken effect that you can feel below the surrounding surface.

You’ll find it on business cards, book covers, leather goods, luxury packaging and rigid boxes. It makes logos and key details noticeable without relying on lots of ink. Here is how debossing works, when to use it and how it compares with embossing.

## Why Debossing Matters

A flat printed logo gets attention through color. A debossed logo adds texture customers can feel. Debossing helps you:

- Present your logo cleanly: a recessed logo looks professional and noticeable.
- Add texture: a tactile surface that customers feel in their hands.
- Create depth: the pressed design adds dimension to a flat surface.
- Support minimal designs: simple packaging without busy graphics.
- Elevate presentation: boxes, cards and covers look more refined.

For stronger contrast, debossing can be combined with printing or [foil stamping](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-foil-stamping/).

## How Debossing Works

A custom die is pressed into the material with controlled pressure, and sometimes heat, to make a permanent impression.

1. Prepare the artwork. Choose the logo, pattern, text or symbol to deboss. Simple designs with clear lines work best.
2. Make the die. A custom die is made from the artwork, with its depth and detail set for the effect you want.
3. Position the material. The stock is aligned carefully with the die, since even small misalignment shows.
4. Apply pressure. The die pushes the selected area down. The pressure depends on the material’s thickness and properties.
5. Inspect. Check the depth, alignment and overall look of the finished impression.

## When to Use Debossing

Debossing is ideal when you want to highlight specific elements without making the design busy. Consider it when:

- You want your logo to stand out through texture.
- Your packaging has a clean, minimal look.
- You want customers to physically feel your branding.
- You are designing premium packaging.
- You want to highlight a brand name, pattern or short text.
- You want an alternative to printed graphics.
- Your design already uses foil or other decorative finishes.

It works especially well where customers touch the surface, such as a debossed logo on the lid of a [rigid box](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/rigid-boxes/). Very small text or highly detailed artwork may not deboss clearly, so review your artwork before production.

## Embossing or Debossing: Which Is Better?

[Embossing](https://packlegacy-website.vercel.app/blog/what-is-embossing/) raises artwork above the surface; debossing presses it in. Neither is automatically better; it depends on the look you want.

Choose embossing when you want the design to stand out physically, give your logo more prominence or create a noticeable 3D effect.

Choose debossing when you want a subtle, recessed design, a minimal look, depth without raising the surface, or understated branding.

Both can be paired with foil stamping or printing for extra contrast.

## Conclusion

Debossing adds texture, depth and a physical element to logos and artwork on packaging and print. It is especially effective when your design calls for a clean, subtle, tactile finish.
